# internalQueryMaxScansToExplode and maxScansToExplodeReached

# internalQueryMaxScansToExplode and maxScansToExplodeReached — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for internalQueryMaxScansToExplode and maxScansToExplodeReached. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] The ESR guide describes fewer than 201 $in elements as eligible for expansion and SORT_MERGE when used with sort, and 201 or more as range-like for following index sort fields. It explicitly warns that this boundary is not guaranteed across versions; the scan-product logic further scopes that simplified single-array rule. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/ · keywords: internalQueryMaxScansToExplode and maxScansToExplodeReached · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The inspected v8.0 planner multiplies point-interval counts across exploded prefix fields and sums counts across explodable nodes. Thus two eligible prefix fields of one index scan with 20 and 11 point intervals need 220 scans, exceeding a 200 limit. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp · keywords: internalQueryMaxScansToExplode and maxScansToExplodeReached · also: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37834717/how-to-query-and-sort-data-with-2-in-operators-using-only-index-covered-query
- [statement] A false maxScansToExplodeReached flag does not prove SORT_MERGE eligibility: expansion can fail earlier on bounds, multikey metadata, collation, or sort compatibility. Inspect winningPlan to determine the selected sort strategy. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp · keywords: internalQueryMaxScansToExplode and maxScansToExplodeReached · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/explain.cpp
- [statement] Lim Jong Eun's April 2024 engineering article demonstrates a three-value $in producing three IXSCAN children under SORT_MERGE, with executionStats tracing the work. Its limit discussion uses MongoDB r4.4.23 code; its experiment is independent of the vendor documentation. (low confidence) — https://medium.com/@zl2-/mongodb-in-or-sort-%EC%BF%BC%EB%A6%AC%EC%99%80-sort-merge-%EB%8B%A8%EA%B3%84-479bf8d53ac6
- [statement] The v8.0 threshold comparison is strictly greater-than: exactly 200 generated scans do not fail this check at the default setting; 201 do. Passing this check alone does not guarantee that the optimizer selects SORT_MERGE. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp · keywords: internalQueryMaxScansToExplode and maxScansToExplodeReached · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/query_knobs.idl
- [statement] Lim Jong Eun's April 2024 worked example shows a three-value $in producing three IXSCAN branches under SORT_MERGE. Its executionStats return 10 documents after examining 12 keys, illustrating the value of merging individually ordered scans when a small limit permits early termination; those counts belong to that example. (low confidence) — https://medium.com/@zl2-/mongodb-in-or-sort-%EC%BF%BC%EB%A6%AC%EC%99%80-sort-merge-%EB%8B%A8%EA%B3%84-479bf8d53ac6

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] When the v8.0 expansion count exceeds the operation's scan limit, explodeForSort sets hitScanLimit and returns false. The inspected explain serializer exposes hitScanLimit as queryPlanner.maxScansToExplodeReached, a planning-limit Boolean rather than an execution scan counter. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp · keywords: internalQueryMaxScansToExplode and maxScansToExplodeReached · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/explain.cpp, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [statement] Raising the knob increases the permitted expansion work; it does not remove other sort-eligibility checks. The planner's own reason for the cap is that excessive index scans hurt performance. Treat a higher setting as a workload-specific experiment rather than a universal optimization. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/query_knobs.idl · keywords: internalQueryMaxScansToExplode and maxScansToExplodeReached · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp, https://medium.com/@zl2-/mongodb-in-or-sort-%EC%BF%BC%EB%A6%AC%EC%99%80-sort-merge-%EB%8B%A8%EA%B3%84-479bf8d53ac6
- [statement] SERVER-83777 links inclusion of $in length in the plan-cache key to explodeForSort and caps that length at internalQueryMaxScansToExplode + 1. The ticket lists fixes in 7.0.5, 7.2.1 and 7.3.0-rc0; it concerns cache-key cardinality rather than raising the expansion cap. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-83777

## Facts and statements

- [statement] In MongoDB v8.0, internalQueryMaxScansToExplode limits how many index scans explodeForSort may generate to obtain sort order. Its declared default is 200; the parameter accepts nonnegative integers and is settable at startup and runtime. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/query_knobs.idl · keywords: internalQueryMaxScansToExplode and maxScansToExplodeReached · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-83777
- [statement] Andrey Hohutkin's June 2016 report describes a compound {userId:1, action:1, time:-1} index where the product of user and action counts crossing 200 caused loss of a fast covered SORT_MERGE plan. This is a historical workload observation, not a current-version benchmark. (low confidence) — https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37834717/how-to-query-and-sort-data-with-2-in-operators-using-only-index-covered-query
- [statement] SERVER-113079 records a customer case where changing internalQueryMaxScansToExplode did not invalidate an existing cached plan, leaving nodes with different plan behavior. The ticket closed as a duplicate on June 4, 2026; this record does not establish which deployed releases retain that behavior. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-113079
- [statement] The v8.0 planner multiplies point-interval counts across explodable prefix fields, then sums the counts across candidate index scans. Thus two eligible $in predicates with 15 distinct point bounds each can require 225 scans, exceeding the default even though neither array has 201 elements. A 2016 independent user report describes this product threshold. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp · keywords: internalQueryMaxScansToExplode and maxScansToExplodeReached · also: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37834717/how-to-query-and-sort-data-with-2-in-operators-using-only-index-covered-query, https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/query_knobs.idl
- [statement] SERVER-130715 records promotion of internalQueryMaxScansToExplode to per-query-shape Persistent Query Settings, with resolution Fixed and fix version 9.0.0-rc1. This ticket supports a 9.0 development change; it does not establish availability of that setting on earlier server versions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-130715
- [statement] A historical cnblogs getParameter listing shows internalQueryMaxScansToExplode: 200 alongside featureCompatibilityVersion: 4.0. This is historical observed parameter output, not evidence for a current server's effective setting or for the version of its binary. (low confidence) — https://www.cnblogs.com/igoodful/p/14943479.html
